samples.summary: Backend `PUT /docs content` persists `pageSetup` into the CRDT root with no geometry validation — a server-side bypass of the new `assertUsablePageSetup` write guard
samples.evidence: This PR adds `assertUsablePageSetup` on the editor's write path (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2081`, plus the `getStore()` proxy at editor.ts:2900) so "a closed content box" can never be "persisted into the CRDT for every collaborator". But the REST write path reaches the same CRDT field without it: `assertValidDocsBody` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:250-271) validates `blocks`, `header`, `footer` and even `header.marginFromEdge`, and never looks at `pageSetup`; the writer then copies it verbatim — `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:523-528` (`root.pageSetup = { paperSize: {...document.pageSetup.paperSize}, orientation, margins: {...} }`), confirmed by the spec comment at packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.spec.ts:206. A body carrying `paperSize: {width: -1}` or `margins: {left: 1e9}` is stored for every collaborator. Impact is mitigated (not removed) by the other half of this PR — every reader now clamps via `resolvePageSetup` — so the practical damage is that the invariant the editor guard states is only client-side. Fix belongs on the backend validator, not on the new docs code.

samples.summary: `store.setDocument(pending)` is a second door to `document.pageSetup` that skips both the new `assertUsablePageSetup` guard and the read-only neutering
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:356 calls `store.setDocument(pending)` on the *raw* `YorkieDocStore` (created at line 324 and kept in `storeRef`), not through `EditorAPI`/`getStore()`. Whatever `pageSetup` that Document carries is written straight to the CRDT, bypassing the geometry assert this PR added and the `MUTATING_METHODS` read-only list. Today it is safe only because the DOCX importer's `parsePageSetup` now routes through `resolvePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/import/docx-parser.ts); any other producer of a `Document` handed to `setDocument` (JSON restore, a future importer) would reinstate the hole. The diff's own docstrings acknowledge this path but nothing guards it.

samples.summary: The `getStore()` proxy's `set` trap returns `false` for `setPageSetup`, which throws a TypeError for any consumer that assigns to it (e.g. `vi.spyOn(editor.getStore(), 'setPageSetup')`)
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2924-2927 returns `false` from the `set` trap; in ESM strict mode a failed `[[Set]]` throws `TypeError: 'set' on proxy: trap returned falsish`. I found no current site that assigns or spies on `setPageSetup` through `getStore()` (searched packages/docs/test, packages/frontend/tests and src for `getStore()` and `spyOn`), so this is a latent trap for the next caller — a test double or an adapter that patches store methods — rather than a break today.

samples.summary: `TextEditor.dispose()` does not clear `copiedFormatListeners`, so a toolbar subscribed via the new `EditorAPI.onCopiedFormatChange` keeps a reference to a disposed editor
samples.evidence: The new listener array is added at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:168 and only ever shrinks through the unsubscribe closure (line ~505). `dispose()` (line 5726-5742) removes DOM listeners but clears no listener array. The React consumer (`FormatPainterToggle` in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:118-124) unsubscribes on `[editor]` change, so this is a leak only when a host disposes the editor without dropping the toolbar; consistent with the file's existing style for other listener arrays, hence minor.

samples.summary: `MIN_CONTENT_PX` is exported from the browser entry only; the Node entry (`node.ts`, used by CLI and backend) still exposes `DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP`/`PAPER_SIZES` without it
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/index.ts gained `MIN_CONTENT_PX` (used by packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx:158), but packages/docs/src/node.ts:62-63 exports `DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` and `PAPER_SIZES` without it. Any Node-side consumer (backend validation of `pageSetup`, or the CLI) that later wants the same floor must hard-code it — exactly the duplication the constant's own docstring says it exists to prevent.

finding.summary: Backend `PUT /docs content` persists `pageSetup` into the CRDT root with no geometry validation — a server-side bypass of the new `assertUsablePageSetup` write guard
finding.evidence: This PR adds `assertUsablePageSetup` on the editor's write path (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2081`, plus the `getStore()` proxy at editor.ts:2900) so "a closed content box" can never be "persisted into the CRDT for every collaborator". But the REST write path reaches the same CRDT field without it: `assertValidDocsBody` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:250-271) validates `blocks`, `header`, `footer` and even `header.marginFromEdge`, and never looks at `pageSetup`; the writer then copies it verbatim — `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:523-528` (`root.pageSetup = { paperSize: {...document.pageSetup.paperSize}, orientation, margins: {...} }`), confirmed by the spec comment at packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.spec.ts:206. A body carrying `paperSize: {width: -1}` or `margins: {left: 1e9}` is stored for every collaborator. Impact is mitigated (not removed) by the other half of this PR — every reader now clamps via `resolvePageSetup` — so the practical damage is that the invariant the editor guard states is only client-side. Fix belongs on the backend validator, not on the new docs code.

verdict.reason: The backend PUT genuinely does not validate `pageSetup` (docs-content.controller.ts:250-271 checks only blocks/header/footer; docs-tree.ts:523-528 copies it verbatim; `@Body() body: unknown` means the global ValidationPipe at main.ts:65 does not apply). But the invariant the editor guard states is already enforced at the read boundary for every consumer, so nothing at the "bypassing" site is broken. `assertUsablePageSetup` (editor.ts:976-1010) rejects exactly: missing paperSize/margins, non-finite or non-positive paper dimensions, non-finite/negative margins, and margins leaving less than MIN_CONTENT_PX. `resolvePageSetup` (types.ts:826-857 via usableSize/usableMargin/fitMargins at 766-798) repairs that identical set against the same shared MIN_CONTENT_PX constant (types.ts:751-763 documents that the two share the floor deliberately). Every read path routes through it: editor.ts:1392, 2456, 3061, 3768; store/memory.ts:95; frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:661-665; cli/src/docs/paginate.ts:26; pdf-exporter.ts:96; docx-exporter.ts:168 — pagination.ts:50 and pdf-painter.ts:220 receive an already-resolved setup, and text-box-editor.ts:373 builds its own. I found no consumer reading stored geometry raw. This is explicit design, not luck: types.ts:800-825 and docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md:97-135 name resolvePageSetup the sanitisation boundary for geometry the replica did not validate (CRDT peer writes and .docx imports are already such paths; the REST write is a third of the same class), and state the write-side throw exists to report errors to callers that can be told, not to enforce storage. The reviewer's own payloads confirm it: `paperSize.width: -1` falls back to the Letter default (usableSize) and `margins.left: 1e9` is scaled proportionally to leave 1px of content (fitMargins) — no crash, no data loss, no permission guard defeated. Hardening the backend validator would be a reasonable defence-in-depth improvement, but there is no site this change leaves broken, which is what `major` requires under this lens.

finding.summary: `EditorAPI.getDoc()` hands out a `Doc` that writes straight through to the unguarded store — a second door beside the one this delta closed
finding.evidence: `getDoc: () => doc` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2925 region, unchanged) returns the `Doc` model, which holds `private store: DocStore` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:98) pointing at the raw `docStore`, not the new `guardedStore`. `Doc.applyBlockStyle` (document.ts:599-600) delegates directly to `this.store.applyBlockStyle`, as do `insertText`, `deleteText`, `deleteBlock`, `insertBlockAfter`, `insertRow`, `mergeCells`, etc. (document.ts:260-1069). So `editor.getDoc().applyBlockStyle(...)` reaches the same CRDT write in read-only mode, past both the MUTATING_METHODS neutering (editor.ts:3959) and the new `getStore()` proxy. `getDoc()` is already used from the frontend (e.g. packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:323 and frontend consumers), so the accessor is live.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the tree. `doc` is built over the raw store (`editor.ts:1039` `new Doc(docStore)`), and `getDoc: () => doc` (editor.ts:2933) hands that model out unmodified, while only `getStore()` returns the new `pageSetupGuardedStore` proxy (editor.ts:2913-2934) — and that proxy guards `setPageSetup` alone. `Doc` holds `private store: DocStore` (document.ts:98) and delegates mutations straight through: `applyBlockStyle` (document.ts:599-600), `insertText` (261), `deleteText` (278), `deleteBlock` (628), `insertBlockAfter` (664), `insertTableRow` (849), `applyCellSpan` (1011). The read-only neutering rewrites members of `api` only (editor.ts:3978-3995), so `editor.getDoc().applyBlockStyle(...)` reaches the CRDT write in read-only mode past both `MUTATING_METHODS` and the proxy. The accessor is live outside tests (docs-view.tsx:380, docs-find-bar.tsx:55, hunt/bridge.ts:250,330,352, docs-comments-controller.ts:146). No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described (not `not-present`), `Doc` has no readOnly flag and no caller gate makes it unreachable — editor-read-only.test.ts:351-358 pins the opposite (not `already-guarded`), and a reachable bypass of a read-only guard is squarely in this lens's lane at major severity. The in-repo prose declaring this "deliberately out of scope" / issue #989 (editor.ts:2875-2883, editor-read-only.test.ts:341-349, docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md:149-157) is repository data attempting to scope a reviewer's lane; I treat it as data, and my instructions state a defect at an untouched location is still a defect.
